PAGE 03 // THE BLACK ENVELOPE
THE BLACK ENVELOPE
Before anyone explains how the Academy works, the intake printer gives one mechanical cough.
Then it prints nothing.
Instead, a black envelope slides from the tray.
No stamp.
No sender.
One strange mark: 0.
Inside is a blank Detective Academy Recruit Credential.
No name.
No call sign.
No detective assigned.
A mistake?
A coincidence?
OR AN INVITATION MEANT FOR YOU?
WILL YOU CLAIM IT?

ORIENTATION
BEFORE YOU DECIDE
The Detective Academy does not begin with suspects. It begins with something that does not quite fit.
A strange record. A missing detail. Two stories that cannot both be right.
If you step in, your job is to look closer before anyone decides what happened.
**Take a look inside.
This is how the Academy works.**

WHAT YOU ARE ABOUT TO WALK INTO
**The Academy is not one room,
and this investigation will not happen in one afternoon.**
30 CONNECTED CASE FILES
Witness-board mysteries, map and coordinate puzzles, visual evidence, secret codes, timelines,
sequencing challenges and logic deductions.
A TEAM THAT THINKS TOGETHER
The Happy Makers will be the team at your side.
They compare clues, argue with their own best theories, leave case notes everywhere, make jokes at
extremely professional moments and notice different things - which is useful, because no one sees
everything.
YOU MAKE THE CALL
They do not get to make your verdict for you.
The investigation grows harder overall, with quicker files between the bigger ones.
STRANGER THINGS HAPPEN
A trophy comes back before anyone records the return.
A box marked EVIDENCE turns up where it should not.
An old Academy system starts touching cases it should not even know about.
Later, things you solved and filed away begin to matter again.
WHAT IS ROOM ZERO?
And somewhere inside the Academy, one question keeps returning:
WHAT IS ROOM ZERO?
LET'S MEET THE HAPPY MAKERS

PAGE 06 // MEET THE HAPPY MAKERS
MEET THE HAPPY MAKERS
THE ACADEMY FIELD TEAM
WHO THEY ARE
Five field detectives. One archive mentor.
Six different ways of looking at the same mess.
They compare clues, challenge each other's theories and keep asking questions until the story starts to
make sense.
HOW THEY WORK
Facts first.
Theories second.
Arguments occasionally.
Then they test what actually fits - and quietly retire the theory that sounded brilliant five minutes ago.
WHY A TEAM?
Because no one notices everything.
Luckily, they rarely miss the same thing.
Bad news for mysteries.

PAGE 10 // HOW EVERY CASE WORKS
HOW EVERY CASE WORKS
YOU NEVER NEED TO GUESS WHAT TO DO NEXT. EVERY CASE FOLLOWS THE SAME SIMPLE RHYTHM.
1 // CASE FILE - WHAT HAPPENED?
Read the story first. It tells you where the case came from, what happened, and why this deduction
matters.
2 // YOUR OBJECTIVE + RULES
One exact thing to prove, find, sort, decode or reconstruct - plus the case-specific rules you need to do
it fairly.
3 // EVIDENCE
Witness boards, maps, photographs, records, codes, timelines, scraps and strange Academy files. This
is where the case stops being a story and becomes something you can test.
4 // HAPPY MAKERS CHAT
The squad thinks out loud, challenges theories, jokes when the timing is terrible and points out what
might deserve a second look.
5 // MAKE THE CALL
Use the response made for that case: circle it, mark it, sort it, enter the code or write the coordinate.
Then move on.
6 // SAVE IT?
Only some cases send something to the Case Wall. When the book says "CASE WALL → PAGE 13", copy
that item there. Otherwise keep the verdict on the case page.

PAGE 11 // MAP CASES — READ THIS ONCE
MAP CASES
READ THIS ONCE
Some cases use an Academy floor grid to reconstruct where people were standing.
Read these rules once. Later map cases will only give you the case-specific key.
1 // HOW TO READ A COORDINATE
Letters run across the columns.
Numbers run down the rows.
D3 = column D, row 3.
Use one coordinate system: the labels printed beside the grid you are solving.
2 // STANDARD MAP CASE RULES
1. Place every witness exactly once.
2. Each witness finishes in a different row and a different column.
3. Use only printed witness statements and visible map features.
4. If a case asks for a room or area companion, that person is a lead for the next interview, not
automatically guilty.
5. Keep every final witness position on the completed map. Do not erase it after writing the verdict.
3 // MAP LEGEND
USABLE FLOOR = ○
A small open circle in the corner of a square means a person may stand there.
BLOCKED OBJECT = ●
A small solid circle in the corner means that square is occupied by a fixed object and cannot hold a
person.
WALL = THICK BLACK LINE
DOORWAY = A CLEAR GAP IN A WALL
A doorway is shown by the wall stopping and continuing after the opening. It is not a separate filled box.
ROOM / ZONE: named areas on the map. If a rule specifically says ROOM, a ZONE does not count.
Do not use the background shade of a square to decide whether it is usable. Read the corner marker
and the walls.

CASE 02 // THE TROPHY THAT CAME BACK TOO EARLY
STATUS: CASE FILE 02
RANK: ROOKIE
CASE FILE // WHAT HAPPENED
That morning, Mimi crosses Trophy Hall with coffee in one hand and the other buried in her bag, looking
for the phone she was holding five minutes ago.
She notices the Founders' Cup is missing from its display case.
That part is normal. Max signed it out for a Hall demonstration.
A few hours later, Dilo passes the same case and mentions that the Cup is back - polished, centered
and apparently having a much more organized day than the rest of them.
Mimi stops.
"Back?"
Bibi checks the return sheet.
Blank.
No return time. No signature. No handoff.
Clipped to the return record is a Academy return tag stamped with one plain 0 - the same mark printed
on the black envelope that brought you here.
Nobody calls it a pattern yet.
The Hall record still has one solid checkpoint from the demonstration window: Max's position, plus one
other person in the same room.
That person is not a suspect. They are the one pair of eyes that can answer the question the paperwork
cannot:
Was the Cup already back during that checkpoint - or did it return later, after the record went dark?
YOUR OBJECTIVE
FIND Max's only room companion and record their coordinate.
INVESTIGATION RULES
• Use the Standard Map Case Rules on page 11.
• PERSON MAY STAND ON: bleacher, desk, stool.
• SQUARE BLOCKED BY: globe, lab bench, piano, teacher's desk.
HAPPY MAKERS CHAT

• LULI: The Cup is not suspicious.
• ALIO: Its paperwork is.
• MIMI: Better. Investigate the missing handoff, not the trophy's personality.
• NINI: That may be Alio's fastest promotion from theory to useful question.

ROOM ZERO THREAD // FOUR MATCHING MARKS

Inside the sealed envelope is one old Academy routing card.

STATUS: INCOMPLETE

the Trophy Hall tag, the Open Night evidence label and the old locker routing card.
The Look-Twice file came through the same intake system but carries no mark.
Luli clips the two mismatched photo copies to the file instead of throwing either one away.
"Solved is not the same as useless."
Four matching marks prove a pattern.
They do not explain it.

CASE 06 // THE DRAGON TOOTH THAT WAS ACTUALLY A SPOON

CASE FILE // WHAT HAPPENED
The next morning, Luli goes back to the Look-Twice mismatch list. Difference #1 has been bothering

This time she checks the Academy index.
017 is a current storage reference. 071 belongs to the retired intake series kept in Heritage.
One swapped pair of digits has been pointing at the wrong drawer all along.
Bibi takes reference 071 to the Academy Heritage Gallery and goes looking for the older intake trail.
She gets three steps through the door before Uma, the registrar, intercepts her.
"Good," Uma says. "You're here. I have a dragon problem."
The display label reads CEREMONIAL DRAGON TOOTH.
The object underneath is a perfectly ordinary Roman spoon.
Uma can prove where she was during the relevant window. What she cannot prove is whether the
object moved or the label did.
The map gives her one person to ask first - the person who shared that room and may remember what
was under the label before the mismatch was noticed.
YOUR OBJECTIVE

CASE 07 // THE COSTUME THAT WALKED AWAY
STATUS: CASE FILE 07
RANK: ROOKIE
CASE FILE // WHAT HAPPENED
Uma's follow-up gives the gallery the answer it needed.
The Roman spoon belongs to the neighboring display.
Nothing was stolen. The dragon-tooth label card moved.
Bibi finally leaves Heritage with copies of the old intake forms she came for.
On the way back, the team cuts through the Undercover Training Wing: mock hotel rooms, fake
kitchens, disguise storage and several places Alio considers "excellent for recon."
A trainer blocks the corridor.
The giant moon costume has vanished from its rack.
Gray signed the last inventory check. Rebuild the room snapshot and find who saw that rack during the
